title: Towards fair decentralized benchmarking of healthcare AI algorithms with the Federated Tumor Segmentation (FeTS) challenge
authors: M. Mongan, U. Baid, S. Pati, M. J. Sheller, G. A. Reina, S. Thakur, et al.
abstract: This study details the outcomes and insights from the Federated Tumor Segmentation (FeTS) challenge, benchmarking decentralized healthcare AI algorithms. It demonstrates that federated learning approaches can construct robust, generalizable segmentation models for neuro-oncology without compromising institutional data privacy.

title: GaNDLF: the generally nuanced deep learning framework for scalable end-to-end clinical workflows
authors: S. Pati, S. Thakur, M. J. Sheller, G. A. Reina, B. Baheti, et al.
abstract: The Generally Nuanced Deep Learning Framework (GaNDLF) is a modular, open-source framework designed to simplify end-to-end clinical workflows for medical image segmentation, classification, and regression. It allows clinical researchers without coding expertise to deploy robust deep learning models across multiple modalities.

title: The federated tumor segmentation (FeTS) tool: an open-source solution to further solid tumor research
authors: S. Pati, U. Baid, M. J. Sheller, G. A. Reina, S. Thakur, et al.
abstract: The FeTS tool provides a user-friendly, desktop-based interface enabling clinical researchers to perform deep-learning-based brain tumor segmentation. Crucially, it facilitates decentralized, privacy-preserving federated training across collaborative research networks without transmitting raw patient imaging data.

title: Clinically Deployed Computational Assessment of Multiple Sclerosis Lesions
authors: S. Thakur, M. Schindler, M. Bilello, S. Bakas
abstract: This study details a clinically deployed deep learning system for segmenting and tracking Multiple Sclerosis lesions in MRI scans. The system improves throughput and segmentation consistency, validated in real-world clinical data pipelines, showing a 90% reduction in processing runtime and decreasing manual diagnostic effort.
